title: Active-set consolidation for KV footprints in long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: Reduce peak GPU residency and fragmentation caused by per-request KV allocations for long-context workloads across Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants by consolidating the active KV working sets.
details:
Background: Long-context requests (>=32k tokens for some Qwen/Llama flavors) create transient but large KV footprints. Current allocator creates many short-lived shards which increases fragmentation and forces conservative over-allocation for safety. This ticket explores an 'active-set consolidation' approach: group and compact co-resident KV slices using stride-aware sharding, residency windowing, and eviction hysteresis to reduce peak memory and amortize KV overhead across in-flight batches.

Scope: Prototype allocator + runtime heuristic changes for hosted and dedicated modes; bench on Llama-2-70B-long, Mistral-1.1-24k, Qwen-2-7B-32k variants. Ensure correctness for quantized kernels and zero-copy KV mappings used by the runtime.

Key ideas: 1) Stride-aware sharding: align KV slices to a stride grid per-variant to increase coalescing potential and reduce padding. 2) Active residency windows: maintain per-request residency windows that allow short-lived overlaps to be compacted rather than immediately evicted. 3) Eviction hysteresis and bloom hints: avoid thrashing by requiring eviction score to exceed hysteresis threshold; use probabilistic hints for collision candidates. 4) Slab hint profiles per-model-variant: supply variant profiles from onboarding to bias allocation sizes and alignment.

Success criteria: - Peak GPU memory reduction >= 10% on targeted long-context mixes without >5% tail latency regression. - No regression in correctness or decoding outputs. - Integration tests for quantized variants pass in CI and nightly dedicated infra runs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Bench harness runs available for three model variants showing peak mem, p95/p99 latency, and throughput before/after. 2) Rollout plan with canary on dedicated pool and fallback to previous allocator. 3) Automated correctness checks (repro seeds) pass for generation and chat flows.
plan:
Phase 1 (week 1-2): implement stride-aware shard map + simple consolidation pass in allocator simulator; unit tests and microbenchmarks. Phase 2 (week 3-4): integrate to runtime, add residency window state and eviction hysteresis, run large-model benches on CI GPU pool. Phase 3 (week 5): telemetry and rollout (canary, A/B), dashboarding for peak memory and eviction churn.

Rollout: start with Mistral-1.1-24k on dedicated dev pool, then Llama-2-70B-long, then Qwen-2-7B-32k. Canary policy: 5% traffic then 25% then full with automatic rollback on memory SLO breach.
notes_and_tradeoffs:
Trade-offs: Aggressive consolidation reduces peak but can increase p95 if consolidation delays allocation for new requests; eviction hysteresis trades memory headroom for stability. Implementation complexity increases allocator state and GC-style compaction epochs which may interact with continuous batching. Quantized KV layouts require careful alignment to avoid extra copies.

Alternatives considered: global compacting GC (too intrusive), conservative over-allocation (cheap but wasteful), and model-level pinning (good for dedicated but poor for shared-hosted).
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for shard alignment and eviction scoring. 2) Regression suite for generation outputs using canonical prompts and seeds. 3) Nightly full-model runs that compare memory traces and KV residency heatmaps. 4) Chaos tests: simultaneous bursts and long-decoding sessions to validate hysteresis.
perf_expectations: Preliminary simulator runs: Mistral-1.1-24k peak GPU mem -12%, Llama-2-70B-long -9%, Qwen-2-7B-32k -15% on mixed batch workloads. Expected throughput change: +/-3% depending on batch mix. Latency tail impact: +1-4% p95 in worst mixes before hysteresis tuning. These are preliminary and will be validated in Phase 2.
risks: Increased allocator complexity causing regressions under high concurrency
Unexpected interaction with continuous batching that increases token latency
Quantized copy overhead if alignment rules collide with kernel requirements
mitigations: Sandboxed canary rollout and automatic fallback
Detailed telemetry (eviction churn, compaction epochs, alignment pad distribution)
Conservative defaults for hosted tier, more aggressive configs for Dedicated
